newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lockheed eyes European aircraft deals.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed eyes European aircraft deals.

text.p: Lockheed Martin Corp. is holding talks with partner firms in Europe's Airbus Industrie about designing and building a large military aircraft, a senior Lockheed executive said.

Lockheed Martin is the largest U.S. military contractor and makes combat planes, rockets, satellites and other high-technology gear. It is looking to diversify into international markets by joining with foreign companies.

An Airbus Industrie project to build an in-flight refueling tanker was one of the planes the U.S. company has been discussing, James Blackwell, president of Lockheed Martin's aeronautics sector, said at the Paris airshow.
"That's one of the projects we have talked about," he said in an interview on Saturday.
But Airbus has not made a firm decision to go ahead with the project, he said. The tanker plane would meet the U.S. government's need for a replacement for the KC-135 aircraft.

A related area of possible cooperation was a replacement plane for the U.S. strategic military transporter C141, Lockheed Martin spokesman Lee Whitney said. The U.S. company has been talking to both Airbus and Aerospatiale, the French partner in Airbus, as well as the other partners, he said.
There were no deadlines for the talks and no decisions have been made, he said.
Lockheed Martin is also interested in bidding to supply engine parts to two key Airbus planes planned for its A340 line of long-range jetliners, the A340-500 and 600, Blackwell said.

But Airbus has not yet chosen the engines for the new A340 models, which are planned as its stop-gap product against archrival Boeing's 747 jumbo jet, until it launches its high-capacity jet, the A3XX, which would seat 500 passengers.

Lockheed Martin is also keen to make parts for the A3XX, which is being studied by Airbus, but Blackwell ruled out for the time being becoming a risk-sharing partner in the project, whose development costs are expected to be at least $8 billion. "I'm not interested in buying shares," he said.
Lockheed Martin is happy to be a subcontractor in commercial aircraft selling aircraft parts to Airbus and Boeing, rather than being a prime contractor, he said.
